title: Chunky throw shawl
subtitle: A top-down triangle in super-chunky treble stitch, worked in a single colour on a 10 mm hook
excerpt: This top-down triangular shawl grows from a four-chain foundation to 140 cm wide and 65 cm deep in super-chunky yarn on a 10 mm hook. Each row adds two trebles, one on each side of the central spine. The resulting fabric is thick and cosy. Suitable for crocheters who know the treble stitch.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Top-down triangular shawl construction from a central spine is a widely documented technique with no single source.

glossaryTerms.definition: The single stitch at the centre of a top-down triangular shawl. One treble is placed on each side of the spine on every row, so the shawl grows symmetrically on both halves.
For treble stitch, a ch-3 at the start of a row stands in for the first treble. The final stitch of the next row is worked into the top of this chain, keeping the stitch count consistent.

content.text: This triangular shawl starts at the top centre and grows downward on a 10 mm hook in super-chunky yarn. The construction is straightforward: each row begins with a ch-3 turning chain, works trebles to the central spine stitch, places one treble on each side of the spine to create the increase, and continues to the end of the row. After roughly 33 rows the triangle reaches the finished dimensions.
The
spine stitch
sits at the exact centre of every row. Mark it with a stitch marker and move the marker up on each row so you can always find the centre without counting across. The
turning chain
of ch-3 counts as the first treble on every row.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 500 g super-chunky weight yarn. A 10 mm crochet hook (US N/P 15). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Stitch marker. Tape measure.

content.text: Gauge

8 tr x 5 rows = 10 x 10 cm in super-chunky yarn with a 10 mm hook, measured unstretched. Work a swatch of 12 stitches and 7 rows and measure the central 10 x 10 cm. At this scale, one stitch per 10 cm changes the finished width by about 18 cm, so it is worth checking before beginning.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
Pattern
The shawl is worked flat. The ch-3 turning chain counts as the first treble on every row. Place a stitch marker in the centre spine stitch and move it up on every row.
Foundation chain
Ch 4. Place a stitch marker in the 2nd ch from the hook. This is the centre spine chain.
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in the 4th ch from hook. 2 tr in the marked spine ch. 1 tr in the last ch. Turn. (5 sts)
Row 2

Ch 3 (counts as first tr). 1 tr in each st to 1 st before the spine st. 2 tr in the st before the spine. 1 tr in the marked spine st (move marker to this st). 2 tr in the st after the spine. 1 tr in each st to end, working the final tr into the top of the turning ch. Turn. (7 sts)
Rows 3 to 33

Repeat Row 2 on every row. Two stitches are added on each row (one on each side of the spine). After Row 33 you have 69 sts, the shawl is approximately 140 cm wide and 65 cm deep. Move the marker up each row to keep track of the spine.

attrs.title: Adjusting the size
attrs.body: Each additional row adds approximately 2.5 cm to the width (1 tr each side at the stated gauge). Work more rows for a larger shawl or fewer for a smaller one.

content.text: Cast-off row

After the final row, do not turn. Work 1 dc (UK) along the top straight edge to neaten: join with sl st at the top left corner, work 1 dc in each stitch along the foundation chain edge, sl st to the starting corner. Fasten off.
Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends. Thread each tail through the tapestry needle and pass it through the backs of several stitches. Super-chunky yarn does not need aggressive blocking. Lay the shawl flat, ease gently to the stated dimensions, cover with a damp cloth, and allow to dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with a gentle wool wash. Press out excess water gently and lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry or hang while wet, as the weight of chunky yarn will distort the shape.
What to try next

Work the same top-down triangle construction in DK on a 4 mm hook for a finer, lighter shawl with more rows. Add a simple shell-stitch border along both diagonal edges after the last row. A striped version using two contrasting super-chunky colours changes shade every four rows for a bold block effect.
